title: ConPTY host failure and teardown acceptance
canonical_summary: Strengthen the existing process-host gate with independent channel progress, partial-startup cleanup and version-aware teardown acceptance, preserving truthful completion and output availability.
gui_classification_reason: Process-host correctness and native acceptance; no visual presentation or new user flow is added.
negative_constraints: No new engine, FFI, DLL distribution, OS support or numeric timeout selection.
No output loss rewriting known completion, API-return finality assumption, or rollback of executed effects.

title: Represent required command-block history without fabricated facts
canonical_summary: Align required nullable command-block history and qualified outcomes with one registered v2 value, exact legacy preservation and coordinator-owned conversion under the existing storage migration contract.
gui_classification_reason: Not GUI: storage representation, provenance and migration; direct visual behavior remains owned by existing consumers.
negative_constraints: No restored history becoming live runtime authority.
No raw secret-bearing command/cwd text, fabricated ordinals/markers/completion, or silent unversioned shape drift.
No ordinary mixed-version steady state or unprotected original rewrite.
Synthetic fixture versions do not allocate a production store edge or waive application ceilings.
Observed status=null and later backing loss do not erase source-qualified completion.
No governance seal, new receipt, global schema revision, engine or feature selection.

title: Align residual FinalGUI retry wording with command owners
canonical_summary: Correct remaining unqualified retry text in FinalGUI to preserve replacement versus same-session rerun versus attachment/presentation recovery, using existing owner behavior.
gui_classification_reason: Visible terminal card actions, reuse and invocation identity are directly specified.
negative_constraints: No new terminal/session/card or command replay for attachment/presentation recovery.
No terminal actions introduced into web/search/diff cards.
No new command or runtime authority.
